newsitem.title: FRANCE: Traders call bid truce after EU raises wheat tax.
newsitem.headline: Traders call bid truce after EU raises wheat tax.

text.p: The latest European Union increase in its wheat export tax has -- as widely expected -- driven away all further bids through France today, grain officials said.
They said no bids had been received for soft wheat export licences after the Commission doubled its tax to six Ecus earlier on Thursday.
An EU farm official said earlier the tax would discourage bidding, but was not designed to prohibit all sales.
Thursday's pause in bidding marks a truce after a week of hostilities between the Commission and traders who had seen over a million tonnes of export bids rejected yet kept coming back for more.

Traders were awaiting news about the fate of 472,000 tonnes of bids presented on Tuesday and Wednesday, at the previous tax of three Ecus, and which are still in suspense despite signs the EU will nod them through.
The Commission has until Friday to decide on bids submitted on Tuesday, and Monday for those sent in on Wednesday.
Under its rules, it only needs to respond to bids when it wants to reject them. Doing nothing would mean they were accepted automatically.
In practice, grain officials and traders said the fact there had been indication at least that Tuesday's bids had foundered meant the whole set would probably go through.
A Commission spokesman said earlier bids for 472,000 tonnes had been accepted "in principle".
This was an unusual caveat but officials did not see a deliberate challenge to the bids, which would most likely be accepted along with small quantities of durum and wheat flour.
